title: How to turn your Airbnb into a passive income stream
summary: If your Airbnb feels more like a second job than an investment, you're missing a system. Discover the 4 key areas to automate for passive income.
body_text: How to turn your Airbnb into a passive income stream by Guesty Marketing Team | July 30, 2026 Reading time: 7 minutes Share Guesty Marketing Team Share If you’re still answering “what’s the wifi password?” at 10 PM, your Airbnb isn’t passive income. It’s a second job. The dream of earning money while you sleep gets replaced by the reality of managing bookings, coordinating cleanings, and adjusting rates across multiple websites. You can get your time back. Achieving passivity requires building a system, not just flipping a switch. It’s a spectrum. You move from active, hands-on management to a mostly automated, hands-off state by building a system. This guide shows you how to build that system, step by step. TL;DR Airbnb income is rarely 100% passive from the start; it’s a business that requires systems to run itself. For tax purposes, the IRS generally considers short-term rental income “active” if you materially participate in operations. The path to passive income involves automating four key areas: guest communication, operations, pricing, and distribution. Automating guest messages for common questions and scheduling check-in instructions are the first and biggest time-savers. Syncing your calendars with a channel manager prevents double bookings and eliminates manual updates on Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo, and Expedia. A remote team of cleaners and a reliable handyman are essential for hands-off property management. A vacation rental software like Guesty® connects all these automations, turning a second job into a real asset. Is Airbnb income truly passive? The short answer is no. True passive income requires little to no daily effort to maintain. Think stock dividends or bond interest. An Airbnb, by contrast, is an operating business. Guests have questions, cleaners need schedules, and properties require maintenance. Without a system, you are the system. Instead of a simple yes/no, think of it as a passivity spectrum. Active Management (Manual) Semi-Passive (Some Automation) Passive Management (System-Driven) You answer every guest message personally. You use saved replies for common questions. Automated messages and AI handle 90% of guest communication. You text your cleaner after each checkout. You have a shared calendar for turnovers. Cleaning tasks are automatically created and assigned at checkout. You manually update prices on each OTA. You use a basic dynamic pricing tool. AI adjusts your rates 24/7 across all channels. You meet guests to hand over keys. You use a lockbox with a changing code. Smart locks generate unique codes for each guest automatically. Your goal is to move from the left column to the right. Moving from the left column to the right frees up your time and can also change how your income is treated by the IRS . Understanding the IRS: Active vs. passive rental income The IRS has specific rules about what counts as passive income, and it often comes down to “material participation.” If you provide substantial services like cleaning, concierge services, or frequent guest interaction, the IRS will likely classify your Airbnb income as active. This means it’s subject to self-employment taxes. If you significantly reduce your involvement by using automation and hiring third-party services, you may be able to classify the income as passive. This is a complex area, and the rules depend on how many hours you spend and the nature of your involvement. Always consult a tax professional to understand your specific situation. 4 steps to make your Airbnb hosting more passive Moving your business along the passivity spectrum requires a deliberate, four-part strategy. Focus on automating the most repetitive, time-consuming tasks first. Step 1: Automate your guest communication Guest messaging is the single biggest time drain for most hosts. It’s also the easiest to automate. Your goal is to answer every common question before the guest even asks. Start by scheduling automated messages for key moments in the guest journey, such as a booking confirmation to verify details, a pre-arrival message with check-in instructions, a mid-stay check-in to ensure everything is okay, a pre-checkout reminder, and a post-stay message requesting a review. Boost your short term rentals today Get started To manage this, you need a single place to see all conversations. A Unified Inbox pulls messages from Airbnb, Vrbo, and your email into one feed, so you’re not switching between apps. For the next level of automation, AI agents can take over. Guesty’s ReplyAI agent, for example, can read incoming messages, understand their intent, and send a personalized reply based on your business rules, handling the conversation for you. Step 2: Streamline your operations and turnovers The physical management of your property is the next frontier of automation. This means coordinating cleanings, maintenance, and guest access without your direct involvement. Automate Cleaning Schedules: Connect your booking calendar to your cleaner’s schedule. A vacation rental software can automatically create a cleaning task and assign it to your cleaner the moment a guest checks out. With a platform that supports Tasks Management , your cleaner can even upload photos of their work for quality control. Automate Guest Access: Installing a smart lock eliminates key handoffs and lockbox issues. You can generate a unique access code for each guest that activates at check-in and expires at checkout. For compliance, always disclose the use of smart locks and any exterior security cameras in your listing description and house rules. Automate Maintenance: Create a system for handling repairs. Give a trusted local handyman their own access code and permission to handle issues up to a certain cost without needing your approval. Step 3: Optimize your pricing and bookings Manually adjusting your prices and calendars is a recipe for lost revenue and burnout. If you list on more than one platform, you also risk double bookings. This is where automation becomes critical for your bottom line. First, stop updating calendars by hand. A Channel Manager syncs your availability in real time across Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo, and Expedia. When a guest books on one channel, the dates are instantly blocked on all others. No more frantic calls to resolve a double booking. Second, automate your pricing strategy. A dynamic pricing tool automates your entire rate strategy. An AI-powered tool like Guesty PriceOptimizer™ acts as your personal revenue manager, analyzing market demand, local events, competitor pricing, and historical data to adjust your rates 24/7. It finds revenue opportunities you would have missed, ensuring you’re never underpriced on a busy weekend or overpriced on a slow Tuesday. Step 4: Build your remote support team Automation handles the digital work, but you still need reliable people for the physical tasks. A strong remote team is the final piece of the passive income puzzle. Your core team should include: A Primary Cleaner: Someone who understands your standards and can act as your eyes and ears on the ground. A Backup Cleaner: Essential for when your primary cleaner is sick or unavailable. A Handyman: For everything from a leaky faucet to a broken appliance. Vet them thoroughly, create detailed checklists, and pay them well. These professionals are what allow you to manage your property from anywhere in the world. The right tech stack: your engine for passive income You can buy a smart lock, use a separate pricing tool, and email your cleaner. But disconnected tools create more manual work, not less. You end up managing the tools instead of the business. A truly passive system requires a single, integrated platform that connects every part of your operation. Guesty® is a vacation rental management software that acts as the central engine for your business. It runs your automated messaging, creates your cleaning tasks, syncs your calendars, and optimizes your pricing from a single dashboard. When your communication, operations, and revenue tools talk to each other, the system runs itself. That’s when your Airbnb stops being a second job and starts becoming a true income-generating asset. title: Choose better SaaS with a software evaluation checklist
summary: Use our software evaluation checklist as a template to make your SaaS buying process easier.
body_text: Whether you're a procurement professional or a department owner, each time buying a new SaaS product can feel like the first time. Tech specs, licensing agreements, contract terms: how do you know if you're getting the best deal? Adding a software evaluation template to your purchasing toolbox can simplify the process. This post will explain the software evaluation process to help you make the best SaaS purchase for your business and provide a software evaluation checklist for you to use for your next purchase. {{cta1}} What to include in your software assessment checklist You've gone through all the initial software buying steps and are ready for product evaluation and selection. Let's walk through a list you can customize and use as a software evaluation criteria template. Here's what this software review template ensures: The proposed solution meets all required needs You have contacted all customer references The proposed SaaS is scalable The organization has adequate resources to implement the proposed solution There is a consensus among the critical stakeholder team Free software evaluation template: Outline your company's software purchasing process and empower stakeholders to efficiently identify needs, evaluate options, and request SaaS solutions using this downloadable guide . The proposed solution meets all required needs Do research and collaborate with key stakeholders inside your company to ensure the SaaS solution meets your business needs. In your software vendor evaluation template, you should start with: Competitive market research Align business needs with internal stakeholders Next, your software selection template should include a detailed list of all required and desired usability specifications. Those specifications range from superior functionality needs to implementation and data security to ongoing customer support. Develop a list of required and desired specifications Functionality specifications, like User-friendly and intuitive Custom data collection forms Automated workflows Technical specifications, like Must work with other existing solutions (CRM, ERP, online forms, etc.) Single sign-on Security and privacy specifications, like Supplier must complete a company security questionnaire and demonstrate best security practices Supplier must maintain SOC 2 certification , and GDPR compliance Supplier must participate in regular security audits Must include a data privacy policy in the proposal Must specify guaranteed uptime with a two-year history of uptime metrics Cost specifications like Pricing is itemized and inclusive unless otherwise specified as add-ons Supplier must provide all pricing model options Implementation specifications, like The proposal must include all required implementation needs from the supplier and company in the proposal Supplier must provide a detailed implementation timeline Customer support specifications, like Supplier must demonstrate excellence in customer satisfaction Supplier must provide details of the support team dedicated to the company account Supplier must have mechanisms to accept and resolve customer feedback quickly You have contacted customer references for the potential supplier and their proposed solution For this section, you must: Request references comparable to your organization Contact the reference via email Let them know who you are, why you're reaching out, and what you'd like to discuss with them. If the supplier listed is not the correct person to speak to, they can involve the appropriate people. Set up a call to ask questions and learn more about your proposed solution's successes, ease of use, and other concerns. When designing your software tool evaluation template, you can include specific questions for your customers to receive standardized feedback. The proposed SaaS is scalable enough to meet your firm’s needs It is important to define goals for the software in the future, both short and long-term. These goals should be part of your evaluation checklist. Perhaps your intentions are for this solution to expand from one department's use to enterprise use. Or, maybe you'll need to expand this solution from internal to external customer use, too. If your plans include growth, include scaled needs in your software evaluation report. Outline the following future-proof tasks in your software product evaluation template: Anticipate your software needs 3, 6, 12, and 24 months from now Propose various use cases to your software salesperson Assess the opportunities to scale up or scale down your use of the product The organization has adequate resources to implement the proposed solution It isn't uncommon for a SaaS implementation to require dedicated implementation resources within the company, especially if it's an enterprise solution. At least one, if not multiple, IT representatives may be needed for any software system. Include the following in your technical software evaluation template: IT has the team members available to dedicate to your project You have hired project managers or third-party consultants for implementation Establish a consensus among the critical stakeholder team Next, ensure that all stakeholders agree on the best solution and supplier for the business. Your software selection criteria template should include consensus drivers like Established evaluation criteria scoring, ‘brass tacks’ requirements A process for stakeholders to share this information Agreed-upon product evaluation forms that are clear and easy to complete A straightforward process for assessing the winning criteria A process to share the evaluation report with the team The next steps to move the deal into procurement and implementation Vendr is the buy button for SaaS Choosing the software you need is the vital part. Purchasing it isn’t the best use of your time. Vendr buys software for you and gets the best price, keeping you in the loop the entire time. As SaaS needs continue to grow and change, the art of SaaS buying must become even more versatile, dynamic, and flexible. SaaS buyers should simplify processes to free up time to focus on things that will benefit their business. ‍

title: Churchill Downs Team Members Give Back Through Food Pantry Volunteer Effort
summary: The post Churchill Downs Team Members Give Back Through Food Pantry Volunteer Effort appeared first on Churchill Downs .
body_text: Churchill Downs Team Members Give Back Through Food Pantry Volunteer Effort Jul 20, 2026 Churchill Downs team members partnered with Catholic Charities of Louisville to support the Father Jack Jones Food Pantry. They served on Wednesday mornings throughout May and June to help fight food insecurity in our community. Each week, volunteers rolled up their sleeves and assisted with a variety of essential tasks that help the pantry serve local families and individuals in need. From unloading deliveries and organizing inventory to setting up for distribution, assisting clients, and cleaning up, our team was proud to contribute. The Father Jack Jones Food Pantry plays a vital role in providing nutritious food and resources to members of the South Louisville community, and it was inspiring for our volunteers to see firsthand the impact of these services. Through their time and effort, Churchill Downs team members helped support an operation that serves hundreds of families while fostering meaningful connections with fellow volunteers and community members. Volunteerism is an important part of Churchill Downs' commitment to strengthening the communities where we live and work. Opportunities like this allow our team members to make a tangible difference while supporting organizations that are creating positive change across Louisville.
